long_biography.plain_text:
At Labelle Downs, Peter Robert Camm’s work extended beyond owning land to the mechanics of running a remote cattle station. When a public-road proposal crossed the property, he argued that moving the route would require a new causeway and complicate the trucking and mustering of tens of thousands of cattle.

His pastoral interests also included Natal Downs, a long-established North Queensland run with records dating to the nineteenth century. Camm donated one of its historical worker ledgers to James Cook University’s Delamothe Collection, preserving material from the station’s working life between 1937 and 1944.
